summary: Console alert export truncates trace identifiers after time-range shift, causing broken trace links
description:
Issue summary: Customers report that Alert CSV exports produced from the console contain truncated trace identifiers after changing the dashboard time range. The truncated IDs no longer resolve in the trace viewer, causing 404s and breaking incident investigation workflows.

Impact: Arcadia Retail (dedicated) uses exported alert CSVs to attach trace links into their internal ticketing system. Since 2026-03-09 afternoon, exported rows have trace IDs that are 16 characters shorter than expected; clicking the trace link from the console or the CSV results in a 'Trace not found' error. This prevents timely root-cause analysis during alerts and blocks their on-call playbooks.

Environment: prod | us-east, console v2.14.1, export-service v1.6.2. Affected orgs are on dedicated capacity; behavior observed only when the console time-range is changed immediately before exporting (e.g., switch from "Last 1 hour" to "Last 24 hours").

Observed behavior: 1) Open Alerts page in console. 2) Switch time range from short window to longer window (<5s gap). 3) Select alerts and export CSV. 4) CSV includes "trace_id" column values that are missing the final 16 characters (truncated). 5) Importing CSV into their ticketing system produces links that fail with Trace 404 in trace viewer.

Expected behavior: Exported CSV should contain the full trace identifiers as displayed in the Alerts UI and links should resolve to the trace viewer consistently regardless of prior time-range changes.

Notes: This appears timing-dependent; some exports (when waiting ~30s after time-range change) produce correct IDs. The front-end displays the full trace link in the UI immediately after the switch, but the exported CSV is generated by a server-side exporter job which seems to receive a partial or stale trace anchor token in certain race conditions.
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Redwood Console (prod, us-east) as an Org Admin for a dedicated org
Navigate to Alerts > Alert history and set time range to 'Last 1 hour'
Click the time range selector and quickly change to 'Last 24 hours'
Select multiple alerts and click 'Export CSV' straight away (do not wait)
Open the CSV and inspect the 'trace_id' column; attempt to open the trace link in the console
logs: 2026-03-09T16:21:12Z console: user change timerange org=arcadia user=ops_lead
2026-03-09T16:21:13Z exporter: wrote csv row for alert_id=al-9821 trace_anchor=anch_01f4a3c9b1e2f3d4
investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging when running console v2.14.1 with export-service v1.6.2 and trace-hook staging flag enabled

Hypothesis: exporter is sourcing trace anchor/token from transient frontend cache value that is overwritten during rapid time-range change. The exporter stores only the first 32 hex chars of the anchor, downstream steps expect 48 chars.
Observed exporter write shows anchor trimmed to 32 chars in server logs; trace-hook logs show 48-char anchor generation immediately prior to change
Frontend shows correct full IDs in UI because UI resolves trace references from local state; server-side export job appears to race against sync of full anchor metadata
No evidence of DB corruption; truncation happens before the CSV write step in exporter process.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Sharma: Customer reported broken trace links in exports; provided reproduction steps and sample CSV attached. Marking P1 due to impact on on-call workflow.
2026-03-10 Miguel Ortega: Assigned for investigation. I'll try to reproduce in staging and instrument exporter to capture incoming anchor payload size.
2026-03-11 SRE - Elena Park: Deployed verbose logging for export-service in staging. Confirmed exporter receives truncated anchor 100% when time-range flip occurs within 2s of export job start.

2026-03-12 Engineering - Aaron Liu: Added a guard in exporter to validate trace_anchor length; if shorter than expected, exporter will retry fetching metadata up to 3 times (hotfix candidate). Preparing PR.

2026-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Communicated workaround to customer: wait 30s after changing time range before exporting. Customer accepted temporary workaround; asked for ETA on patch and release schedule.
resolution: In Progress — temporary workaround provided (wait ~30s after time-range change before exporting). Engineering implemented validation+retry in exporter (PR linked) as hotfix. Next steps: merge PR to release-1.6.x, run canary in us-east for dedicated orgs, and follow with full rollout. Post-release verify exports for sample orgs and update runbook.
follow_up_tasks: Merge exporter length-guard PR and cut hotfix release (release-1.6.3)

Add unit test and e2e test covering rapid time-range switch + export
Update console export telemetry to surface anchor length distributions
Add note to runbook and notify CS/AM teams with guidance
